Testimony of Anya Trundy, Deputy Commissioner Department of Administrative and Financial Services
Testifying in Opposition to

LD 1791, Resolve, to Direct State Agencies to Implement the Social Security Fairness
Act
Sponsored by Rep. Kenneth Fredette Before the Joint Standing Committee on Labor

Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Labor; I am Anya Trundy, a Deputy Commissioner for the Department of Administrative and Financial Services (DAFS) and I am testifying in Opposition to LD 1791 because as far as DAFS
and Maine Revenue Services (MRS) are concerned, there is nothing that needs to be done in response to passage of the Social Security Fairness Act.
MRS reviewed the Social Security Fairness Act last December when Congress first passed it,
just as we do all direct changes to the Internal Revenue Code (IRC) and all tax adjacent federal
law changes, to determine whether they interact with Maine tax law and necessitate a statutory
change. MRS and the Office of Tax Policy staff are experts in their field and are constantly monitoring these sorts of issues as they arise and evolve. Each and every year MRS submits
what is known as `the Conformity Billz" many years this bill simply updates the date in Maine statute through which Maine has conformed to the Internal Revenues Sen/ices Code of 1986, and some years--as we anticipate will be the case as provisions of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act are set to expire at the end of 2025--tax changes at the federal level are numerous and
substantial, requiring the Legislature to consider the extent to which Maine should and can afford to "conform." If the Social Security Fairness Act had necessitated any changes to Maine's tax
statutes, MRS would have identified them and brought them forward in this year's Conformity
Bill, LD 48, which is currently on the Appropriations Table awaiting final passage.
The federal government's elimination of the Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP) and Government Pension Offset (GPO) is a change in how individuai's Social Security benefits are calculated, it is not a change in the tax treatment of Social Security benefits. The additional Social Security benefits that certain individuals have begun receiving as a result of the Social

LD 1791, Resolve, to Direct State Agencies to Implement the Social Security
Fairness Act

Good afternoon Senator Tipping, Chair Roeder and the other distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Labor. l am Bill Brown, Director of Actuarial and Legislative Affairs
for the Maine Public Employees Retirement System (MainePERS).
MainePERS is neither for nor against LD 1791, Resolve, to Direct State Agencies to Implement
the Social Security Fairness Act. We are here to provide information and to offer any assistance
the committee may request surrounding this bill.
Signed into law on January 5, 2025, the Social Security Fairness Act repealed both the Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP) and the Government Pension Offset (GPO). These provisions of
federal law required the reduction of Social Security benefits for individuals who also receive pensions from jobs not covered by Social Security, such as those administered by MainePERS.

There are no actions required of MainePERS to implement the Social Security Fairness Act of
2023. The repeal of the WEP and GPO does not affect MainePERS service retirement benefits.
MainePERS sen/ice retirees will continue to receive their same pension benefit amount. The
WEP and GPO were reductions in Social Security benefits administered by the Social Security
Administration.

MainePERS did have educational materials that referred to the WEP and GPO. These materials already have been updated to reflect the Social Security Fairness Act of 2023. We
have advised MainePERS members to consult with the Social Security Administration for
information about the effect these changes may have on their Social Security benefits. We have
communicated this through our website and through mailings to members. Our Member Sen/ices Representatives also direct members who call, email or visit with questions to the
Social Security Administration for accurate and timely information about their Social Security
benefits.

Thank you for your consideration of this testimony. l am happy to answer any questions. We will
also be available for the work session.
